inventory.method: GitHub GraphQL scan of merged pull requests that close at least one issue, followed by per-revision framework verification
inventory.candidateDefectsMeaning: merged pull requests closing an issue, counted over the 60 most recently updated merged pull requests of the repository
inventory.frameworkVerification: git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout, then git show <revision>:<project file> at every revision named in this record; a repository is never classified by its default branch
inventory.note: no build, no launch and no UI Automation session was run for this record; every entry below is research only

applicationPool.reason: Flow.Launcher/Flow.Launcher.csproj carries UseWPF>true and OutputType>WinExe on net9.0-windows10.0.19041.0 at the candidate revisions, so the window is a real WPF visual tree with native UI Automation peers. Containment: the launcher registers a session-wide hotkey and enumerates Start Menu and installed-program entries, so the worker must own the desktop session; it writes only under its own settings folder

ScreenToGif/ScreenToGif.csproj carries UseWPF>true at every candidate revision inspected, on net6.0-windows and later net8.0-windows10.0.17763.0. Containment: the recorder installs low-level mouse and keyboard hooks and the encoder flows fetch FFmpeg and Gifski on first use, so only editor and options triggers are in bounds and the external encoders must be pre-seeded into the application folder

the Windows head src/app/dev/platforms/desktop/DevToys.Windows/DevToys.Windows.csproj does set UseWPF>true, but the entire user interface is Blazor rendered inside a WebView2 host, so the UI Automation tree exposes a web document rather than WPF automation peers. The 29 entries the winui defect inventory attributed to this repository are not WPF automation evidence for any Windows target

selectedDefects.issueTitle: BUG: System.OverflowException: TimeSpan overflowed in ScrollViewerEx.AnimateScroll
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fix System.OverflowException in CustomScrollViewerEx during Mouse Wheel scroll

frameworkVerified.verifiedAtRevision: 5f9d116708276c1b616edc56c4f95a868f118d4d, on the same branch line as both revisions of this defect

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is a mouse wheel delivered to the result list of a live WPF window, which is exactly the windows-wpf adapter's action path: find the results ScrollViewer through the UI Automation tree, invoke its scroll pattern or synthesise wheel input over its bounding rectangle, and observe whether the process keeps exposing an automation tree. The defect is an unhandled OverflowException raised inside the custom ScrollViewer's animation, so the observable is a window that disappears from the tree on the affected revision and stays present on the fixed one
remaining: build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM with dotnet build and record the exact SDK version
prove process ownership, readiness, reset and cleanup for a launcher that claims a session-wide hotkey
confirm the scroll delta required to overflow the animation duration and minimise it
record a neighbouring legal behaviour: a scroll that does not overflow must keep working on the affected build

selectedDefects.issueTitle: BUG: Unable to cast object of type 'System.Windows.Media.Color' to type 'System.Windows.Expression'
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Refactor InitProgressbarAnimation & avoid style cast issue

frameworkVerified.verifiedAtRevision: 5f9d116708276c1b616edc56c4f95a868f118d4d, on the same branch line as both revisions of this defect

selectedDefects.whySuitable: a WPF-specific failure: the progress bar animation reads a brush colour out of the window style and the styled value is not the expected animatable type, so the exception is raised by the WPF property system while the main window is being composed. The adapter exercises it by opening the launcher window through UI Automation and issuing a query that starts the progress animation, then asserting the window is still in the tree. The failure has no meaning outside a XAML style and dependency-property runtime, which is what makes it WPF evidence rather than generic .NET evidence
remaining: note that this defect's affected revision is the previous defect's fixed revision, so the two must not be scheduled as a single build
identify the minimal query that starts the progress bar animation
build both revisions in the Windows VM and record the SDK version
record a neighbouring legal behaviour where the same window opens without the animation

selectedDefects.issueTitle: BUG: Incorrect language on startup when using system

frameworkVerified.verifiedAtRevision: 5f9d116708276c1b616edc56c4f95a868f118d4d, on the same branch line as both revisions of this defect

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the observable is the Name property of localized WPF elements in the settings window: with the language setting left on 'system', the affected build resolves the wrong resource dictionary and the automation tree reports English labels where the fixed build reports the display-language labels. That is a pure UI Automation tree read against a WPF window and it needs no input beyond opening settings
remaining: decide and record the guest display language, because the trigger depends on the VM's configured UI language and the current guest language is unknown
confirm the divergence is visible in element Name properties rather than only in bitmap text
build both revisions in the Windows VM

selectedDefects.issueTitle: [Bug] Mouse button 5 appears to be displayed as mouse button 3 in recordings
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fix for the second extra color button
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the fix is a one-file change in the WPF editor window's code-behind where the second extra mouse-button colour control is wired to the wrong backing value, so the affected build shows one colour control updating when the other is edited. The adapter drives it entirely through the UI Automation tree of a WPF window: open the editor's mouse-click options, set a value on one colour control, read the value patterns of both controls
remaining: read the diff of Editor.xaml.cs at the fixed revision on the VM and pin the exact pair of controls, since the issue text describes the recorded output while the fix touches the editor options
confirm no recording is needed to observe the swap, otherwise the low-level mouse hook comes into bounds and the trigger must be re-scoped
build both revisions in the Windows VM

build.toolchain: .NET 6 SDK, which is out of support and must be installed explicitly in the guest

selectedDefects.whySuitable: a WPF ResourceDictionary string bound to a button's tooltip is wrong, so the defect is observable as the HelpText or the tooltip element that UI Automation exposes for that button. It is the cheapest possible windows-wpf trigger: open one window, read one automation property, no input synthesis at all, which makes it a good control case next to the input-driven candidates
remaining: confirm the string reaches UI Automation as HelpText or as a tooltip popup element rather than only as rendered pixels
install the .NET 6 SDK in the guest or drop this candidate if the toolchain is refused
build both revisions in the Windows VM
